breakfast.name: Qutab (Thin Stuffed Pancakes)
instructions: Make thin dough, rest 15 min
Mix lamb with onion, salt, pepper
Roll dough very thin, fill half, fold into half-moon
Cook on dry griddle until brown spots appear
Brush with butter, garnish with sumac and pomegranate
breakfast.description: Paper-thin stuffed pancakes — Azerbaijan's iconic street food.

breakfast.name: Dovğa (Yogurt Soup)
instructions: Whisk yogurt with egg and flour
Add rice and 2 cups water
Bring to gentle simmer, stirring constantly
Add chopped herbs
Cook until rice is tender
Serve warm or chilled
breakfast.description: A refreshing herb-loaded yogurt soup served warm or cold.

breakfast.name: Qutab (Stuffed Flatbread)
ingredients: Filling: ground lamb with onion and sumac, OR spinach with onion and pomegranate seeds
instructions: Make simple dough, divide into balls
Roll each ball very thin into a circle
Spread filling over one half
Fold into half-moon, press edges to seal
Cook on dry griddle (no oil) until brown spots appear on both sides
Brush with butter immediately
Serve with sumac sprinkled on top
breakfast.description: Paper-thin stuffed flatbread — the most popular street food in Baku. Meat or herb-filled, always eaten with sumac.

breakfast.name: Dovga (Yogurt and Herb Soup)
ingredients: Fresh herbs: cilantro, dill, mint, spinach, chives (generous amounts)
instructions: Beat yogurt with egg, flour, and rice until smooth
Add to pot with water, stir constantly while bringing to simmer — it will curdle if you stop stirring
Once it simmers without curdling, add finely chopped herbs
Cook 15 min until rice is done and herbs are soft
Can be served hot or cold
Top with a pat of butter
breakfast.description: Azerbaijani yogurt soup thick with fresh herbs — the trick is constant stirring to prevent curdling. Served hot in winter, cold in summer.

lunch.name: Plov (Azerbaijani Pilaf)
instructions: Soak rice 1 hour, parboil until half-done
Brown lamb, add onions and carrots
Layer meat mixture and rice in pot
Top with dried fruits, chestnuts, saffron butter
Cover tightly, steam on low 40 min
Unmold and serve
lunch.description: Azerbaijan's crown jewel — saffron-scented rice with lamb.

lunch.name: Lavangi (Stuffed Fish)
instructions: Clean and butterfly fish
Mix walnuts, fried onions, pomegranate paste, sumac
Stuff fish with walnut mixture
Wrap in foil, bake at 180°C 40 min
Unwrap last 10 min for browning
Serve with lemon
lunch.description: Whole fish stuffed with walnuts and pomegranate — a Caspian delicacy.

lunch.name: Plov (Shah Plov — King's Pilaf)
ingredients: Dried fruits: chestnuts, apricots, raisins, prunes
Gazmag crust: lavash bread or thin dough
instructions: Par-cook rice until half done, drain
Line pot with buttered lavash or thin dough (this becomes the crispy gazmag crust)
Layer rice, mixing some with saffron water for color
In separate pan, cook lamb with dried fruits, chestnuts, cinnamon
Pile saffron rice, then plain rice, then lamb-fruit mixture into crust-lined pot
Cover tightly, cook on very low heat 45-60 min
The gazmag crust should be shatteringly crispy
Invert onto platter — the golden crust is on top
Break the crust tableside
lunch.description: The king of Azerbaijani cuisine — saffron rice with a crispy lavash crust called gazmag, encasing lamb and jeweled dried fruits. UNESCO-listed as intangible cultural heritage.

lunch.name: Dushbara (Tiny Dumplings in Broth)
ingredients: Filling: ground lamb, onion (very finely minced), salt, pepper
instructions: Make firm dough, rest
Roll paper-thin, cut into 2cm squares
Place tiny amount of filling on each — dumplings should be no bigger than your thumbnail
Fold into triangles, press edges, curl ends together
Drop into simmering lamb broth
Cook 8-10 min until they float
Serve in broth with vinegar, dried mint, and garlic on the side
lunch.description: Tiny dumplings in clear broth — the test of an Azerbaijani cook's skill is how small she can make them. Tradition says you should fit a spoonful without counting.

lunch.name: Shah Plov (Royal Pilaf in Crust)
ingredients: Filling: lamb stew with dried fruits (apricots, plums, raisins), chestnuts, saffron, butter
Crust: lavash bread or thin pastry dough
instructions: Parboil rice until half-cooked, drain
Make lamb filling: braise lamb with dried fruits, chestnuts, butter
Line a pot with buttered lavash/pastry, letting sheets overhang the edges
Layer: saffron rice, then lamb-fruit filling, then more rice, then more filling
Fold overhanging lavash over the top to seal completely
Cook on low heat 40-50 min — the lavash crust becomes golden and crispy
Invert onto a serving platter — the dramatic reveal
Cut through the golden crust — steam and saffron aroma escape
The inside is jeweled rice layered with lamb and sweet dried fruits
This is Azerbaijan's royal ceremony dish — the crust-breaking moment is the event
lunch.description: Azerbaijan's crown jewel — saffron pilaf with lamb and dried fruits sealed inside a golden lavash crust and inverted like a cake. The dramatic crust-cutting reveal, where steam and saffron aroma escape, is one of the most theatrical moments in all of food and consistently goes viral. Reserved for weddings and celebrations.

dinner.name: Shah Plov (Royal Pilaf)
instructions: Parboil rice with salt
Line pot with lavash sheets, letting edges hang over
Layer rice, saffron butter, lamb, dried fruits
Fold lavash over top to seal
Bake at 180°C 60 min
Invert onto platter — crispy lavash crust on top
dinner.description: Spectacular pilaf baked inside a lavash bread crust.

dinner.name: Lyulya Kebab
instructions: Mix lamb with onion, herbs, seasoning
Knead until sticky
Mold onto wide flat skewers
Grill over charcoal, turning
Serve in lavash with onions and tomatoes
dinner.description: Char-grilled ground lamb kebabs on flat skewers.

dinner.name: Lavangi (Stuffed Chicken)
ingredients: Filling: 2 cups walnuts (ground), 3 onions (fried until dark), 1 tbsp sour plum paste (alycha) or pomegranate molasses, salt, pepper
instructions: Fry onions until very dark and sweet — this takes 25+ min
Mix with ground walnuts and sour plum paste
Stuff chicken with walnut-onion mixture
Sew or skewer closed
Brush with butter and saffron water
Roast at 180°C for 75-90 min, basting occasionally
The filling absorbs the chicken juices and becomes incredibly rich
dinner.description: Whole chicken stuffed with walnut-onion paste — from the Lankaran region in southern Azerbaijan. The sweet-sour filling is the star.

dinner.name: Lula Kebab
instructions: Mix lamb with grated onion, salt, pepper — knead well for 5 min until sticky
Divide into portions, mold around flat metal skewers into long sausage shapes
The meat must stick to the skewer — if it falls off, knead more
Grill over charcoal, turning every 2 min
Grill tomatoes alongside
Slide kebabs onto lavash bread
Serve with sumac, fresh herbs, and grilled tomato
dinner.description: Ground lamb molded onto skewers and grilled — the art is making the meat stick. Every Azerbaijani mangal-master has their technique.

snacks.name: Pakhlava (Azerbaijani Baklava)
instructions: Layer phyllo with butter and nut mixture
Cut diamonds, place walnut half on each
Bake at 170°C 35 min until golden
Pour honey syrup over while hot
Cool completely
snacks.description: Diamond-shaped baklava with saffron and nuts.

snacks.name: Badimjan Dolması (Stuffed Eggplant)
ingredients: Filling: ground lamb, onion, rice, tomato, herbs (cilantro, mint, basil, dill)
instructions: Hollow eggplants from the top, keep shells intact
Mix lamb with rice, onion, tomato, herbs
Stuff eggplants, replace tops
Stand in pot, pour tomato sauce around
Simmer 35-40 min until rice is cooked through
snacks.description: Stuffed baby eggplants — one of dozens of dolma varieties in Azerbaijan, where dolma is practically a food group.

desserts.name: Şəkərbura (Sweet Nut Pastry)
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, 100g butter, 1/2 cup milk, 1 egg, yeast
instructions: Make yeast dough, rest 1 hour
Grind almonds, mix with sugar and cardamom
Roll dough circles, fill, crimp edges decoratively
Score pattern on top with tweezers
Bake at 180°C 25 min
desserts.description: Ornately decorated crescent pastries filled with spiced almonds.

desserts.name: Shekerbura (Crescent Pastry)
ingredients: Dough: flour, butter, yogurt, egg, yeast
Filling: ground almonds and hazelnuts, sugar, cardamom
instructions: Make rich dough, rest 30 min
Mix ground nuts with sugar and cardamom
Shape dough into thin circles
Fill with nut mixture, fold into crescents
Crimp edges with tweezers or fork in decorative wheat pattern
Brush with egg wash
Bake at 175°C for 18-20 min until golden
desserts.description: Crescent-shaped nut pastry with intricate wheat-ear crimping — made for Novruz (Persian New Year). The pattern is a point of pride.

desserts.name: Pakhlava (Azerbaijani Baklava)
ingredients: Dough: flour, butter, eggs, yogurt, yeast
Filling: ground walnuts or almonds, sugar, cardamom
instructions: Make soft dough, divide into 10-12 balls
Roll each very thin
Layer in buttered tray with nut filling between every 2-3 layers
Score diamond shapes, place clove in each center
Brush with saffron-egg glaze
Bake at 175°C for 35-40 min until deep golden
Pour warm honey syrup over
Let soak several hours
desserts.description: Azerbaijani-style baklava — made with yeast dough instead of filo, giving it a softer texture. Essential for Novruz celebrations.

drinks.name: Azerbaijani Black Tea
instructions: Boil water, warm teapot
Add tea leaves, pour hot water
Steep 5 min
Pour into armudu glass
Serve with sugar cubes, lemon, herbs
drinks.description: Tea served in pear-shaped armudu glasses — Azerbaijan's daily ritual.

drinks.name: Sherbet (Sweet Fruit Drink)
instructions: Dissolve sugar in warm water
Add saffron, steep until golden
Add rose water and lemon juice
Chill, serve with basil leaves
drinks.description: A fragrant sweet drink served at celebrations.

drinks.name: Azerbaijani Tea (Çay)
instructions: Brew strong black tea in a two-pot system (samovar style)
Pour concentrated tea into armudu glasses, dilute with hot water to taste
Place sugar cube between front teeth, sip tea through it — this is the traditional way
Alternatively, stir sugar in
Always serve with jam, sweets, or lemon
drinks.description: Tea is Azerbaijan's national drink — consumed all day, from every glass-shaped armudu. The pear shape keeps the top cool and the bottom hot.

drinks.name: Sherbet (Saffron Rosewater Drink)
instructions: Steep saffron in warm water until deep golden
Make sugar syrup, cool
Mix saffron water with syrup, rose water, lemon juice, cold water
Add soaked basil seeds for texture if desired
Serve ice cold
drinks.description: Golden, fragrant saffron-rose drink — served at weddings and Novruz. The basil seeds add a unique gelatinous texture.
